outline.description: This chapter traces the family’s political background in Colombia, the sequence of intimidation and violence they faced, and the administrative pathway taken through U.S. immigration proceedings, culminating in their appeals to the Tenth Circuit.
subtopics: Jimenez family political background and key incidents of intimidation
Involvement of the Liberal Party and the 2022 Colombian presidential campaign
Threats from political opponents and the narcotrafficking group Don Rafa
Property dispute and resultant violence experienced by the family
Forced migration to the United States without admission or parole
Administrative process: Immigration Judge denial, BIA affirmation, appellate filing

outline.chapter_title: Legal Framework and Standards of Review
outline.description: An overview of the statutory and regulatory basis for asylum and withholding of removal, the evidentiary burden, the required elements of past persecution, the interpretation of well‑founded fear, and the appellate standard applied by the Tenth Circuit.
subtopics: Statistical overview of asylum as discretionary relief under the INA
Definition and enumerated protected grounds in § 1101(a)(42)(A)
Burden of proof and the preponderance standard for asylum
The three‑element test for past persecution (incidents, protected ground, state involvement)
Well‑founded fear of future persecution and its relation to the asylum standard
Withholding of removal: requirement of satisfying asylum elements
Standard of review under 8 U.S.C. § 1252 and the substantial‑evidence test
Appellate review scope over the immigration judge and BIA findings
Dismissal of the petitioners’ due‑process claim as a matter of scope

outline.description: This chapter discusses the court’s application of the persecution threshold, the cumulative effect doctrine, and the evidentiary test for physical, psychological, and emotional harm, culminating in the conclusion that the petitioners’ experiences do not rise to past persecution.
subtopics: Threshold for past persecution: more than mere threats or restrictions
Cumulative effect of multiple incidents in asylum analysis
Analysis of physical, psychological, and emotional harm claims
Court’s application of precedent: Karki, Brandy, Carias‑Mejia, and Chhetri
Rationale for deeming threats alone insufficient for persecution
Evidence supporting the BIA’s conclusion of absent past persecution

outline.chapter_title: Nexus, Government Protection, and Future Persecution
outline.description: Explores the nexus requirement, distinguishing political opinion from criminal affiliation, and evaluates the government unwillingness/unability standard, concluding the petitioners fail to meet the well‑founded fear standard.
subtopics: Nature of the nexus requirement and central reason test
Distinguishing political opinion from criminal affiliation in asylum cases
Role of Don Rafa and the narcotrafficking group in the alleged persecution
Court’s reasoning that Jimenez’s political activity was not the primary motive
Government unwillingness/unability standard: notice, response, and systemic failure
Evaluation of petitioners’ attempts to seek protection and their limited scope
Assessment of the claim that the government would be unable or unwilling to intervene
Court’s conclusion that insufficient evidence exists for a well‑founded fear of future persecution

outline.chapter_title: Safe Relocation, Final Holding, and Significance
outline.description: Describes the safe relocation standard, the court’s assessment of the petitioners’ ability to relocate within Colombia, and the final decision to deny review, plus the broader implications for asylum jurisprudence.
subtopics: Safe relocation standard under asylum law and regulatory guidance
Evidence indicating possible relocation away from the threatened area
Evaluation of the family's ability to relocate within Colombia and mitigate risk
Linkage between failed asylum claim and withholding of removal denial
Overall holding: denial of petition for review and reaffirmation of BIA decision
Legal implications for future asylum applicants: thresholds for threats, nexus, safe relocation
Significance of the case for Tenth Circuit jurisprudence on asylum and withholding
